title: Feature Normalization under Finite Training Budgets
abstract: arXiv:2610.16845v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Standardizing a rare feature can help stochastic gradient descent learn its effect within a finite budget, but it also changes the noise cost of learning. We characterize the lowest rare-subgroup risks attainable by standardized and unscaled training when each chooses a nonnegative constant learning rate and a deterministic stopping time under the same observation cap. For two independent binary features, we derive both optimized risks as prevalence vanishes while the expected number of rare observations remains finite. Uniform control over rates and stopping times reduces each limiting oracle to a scalar minimization. With positive noise, the preferred scaling changes exactly once as we move signal to the rare feature while the limiting risk at initialization stays fixed and positive. The formulas also explain how noise and budget affect the comparison. Separate finite-prevalence bounds favor standardization on a rare-dominant signal fa

translated_title: 有限训练预算下的特征归一化
translated_abstract: 对稀有特征进行标准化可以帮助随机梯度下降在有限预算内学习其效应，但这也改变了学习的噪声成本。我们刻画了在相同观测上限下，当标准化训练与未缩放训练各自选择非负常数学习率和确定性停止时间时，所能达到的最低稀有子群风险。对于两个独立的二元特征，我们在流行率趋于零而稀有观测的期望数量保持有限的情况下，推导出这两种优化后的风险。对学习率和停止时间的一致控制将每个极限预言机简化为一个标量最小化问题。在正噪声存在时，随着我们将信号移向稀有特征，首选的缩放方式恰好改变一次，而初始化时的极限风险保持固定且为正。这些公式还解释了噪声和预算如何影响两者的比较。在稀有主导信号上，有限流行率下的独立界限更有利于标准化。
tldr: 该论文在有限训练预算下理论刻画了标准化与未缩放训练各自可达到的最低稀有子群风险，并据此揭示了噪声水平与训练预算如何决定特征归一化策略的优劣。
en_tdlr: This paper theoretically characterizes the lowest rare-subgroup risks achievable by standardized versus unscaled training under finite budgets, revealing how noise level and training budget determine which feature normalization strategy is preferable.
